text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: gateway cluster 'us-west-gateway' reporting elevated 5xx rate (p95 errors > 6%) and increased backend timeouts for /v1/generate. Investigating. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/batching-hol

alex: acked. i'm on it, pinging oncall.

priya: seeing similar in grafana - gateway latency upward, batcher queue depth on scheduler-3 is spiking.

jamal: @alex @priya oncall? which rotation is it today?

oncall-bot: @alex is the current on-call for inference-svc (shift ends in 35m).

alex: i'm taking triage. can someone drop the relevant query for queue depth and batch wait times?

priya: copying queries. queue depth (per-scheduler):
```sql
SELECT scheduler_id, avg(queue_depth) FROM batcher.metrics WHERE window=1m GROUP BY scheduler_id;
```

priya: batch wait histogram shows a tail at ~800ms for scheduler-3, expected ~50-200ms.

jamal: logs show repeated KV cache growth + eviction churn on scheduler-3. I suspect head-of-line blocking from very large KV entries.

maria: any deploys recently? deploy-bot shows a rolling deploy to batcher v2.18 ~40m ago. No config changes flagged.

alex: ok, playbook step 1: throttle incoming traffic to gateway fallback route to reduce pressure. applying a 30% ingress throttle on us-west-gateway now.

alex: command run:
```bash
aws apigateway update-stage --rest-api-id xxxxx --stage us-west --patch-operations op=replace,path=/throttle, value=0.7
```

alex: throttle applied. routing now ~70% normal. watch for error rate change.

priya: after throttle, 5xx dropped from 6.2% -> 4.1% in 45s. latency p95 still high though.

jamal: we should also lower batcher.max_batch_wait_ms on scheduler-3 to force smaller batches and avoid giant KV cache writes. I'll patch config to 100ms from 500ms.

jamal: patch command:
```yaml
PATCH /api/v1/schedulers/scheduler-3/config
{ "batcher": { "max_batch_wait_ms": 100 } }
```

jamal: applied. watching batch sizes. current avg batch tokens dropped from 1200 -> 220 in last 30s.

maria: i can restart the batch-merge worker on scheduler-3 once sizes stabilize. should we do that?

alex: yes do a rolling restart of batch-merge-worker on scheduler-3, one pod at a time.

maria: restarting pod batch-merge-3a...

maria: pod restarted. logs show startup ok, no crash loops.

priya: KV eviction churn reduced. queue depth falling from 4.8k -> 1.1k in the last 2m. gateway 5xx at 2.0% now.

alex: good. next step: re-enable traffic in measured increments, +10% every 2m while monitoring. I'll coordinate.

alex: +10% -> now 80%

priya: 5xx briefly ticked to 2.8% then back to 2.1%. p95 latency improving.

jamal: i've also pushed a temporary routing policy to route small requests to scheduler-1/2 and heavy-context requests to scheduler-4 to avoid localized saturation.

alex: noted. customer impact: partial degradation for a small % of requests (estimated 6-8% higher latency / 2-3% 5xx at peak). We should prepare an initial customer note.

maria: on it. drafting status update for affected customers and PG.

alex: handing off to @jamal for next 30m, I have another page chain. Keep following the rollback/scale steps if errors rise above 3%.

jamal: taking over. will keep this thread updated. next planned action if regression: scale dedicated batcher pool by +2 instances and enable fallback-to-small-model route.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by alex, assigned to jamal. Priority: P2.

jamal: scaling batcher pool via infra-autoscale now. command:
```bash
kubectl scale deployment batcher-pool-us-west --replicas=6 -n infra
```

jamal: replicas scaled to 6. warming new instances; traffic will shift over next minute.

priya: metrics show queue depth continuing to fall, 5xx now 1.1%, p95 latency within SLO.

jamal: mitigation successful. marking mitigation actions in runbook and adding follow-up ticket to audit KV cache sizing and improve eviction heuristics.

maria: customer note sent to pg and support; no immediate escalations.

alex: thanks team. tagging for postmortem: 
- root cause hypothesis: KV cache growth + large batch sizes causing head-of-line blocking on scheduler-3 after recent deploy
- mitigations: ingress throttling, reduce max_batch_wait_ms, rolling restart of batch-merge worker, routing split, scale pool
- follow-ups: tune eviction, alerting thresholds for batch wait tail, deploy-time canary for batcher config.

jamal: i'll own the postmortem and the follow-up ticket. moving to resolved if metrics stable for 15m.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> Mitigated. Link: https://internal.redwood/incidents/2954321000
